correctness.rationale: The result fixes the real 4-point metric and establishes its exact primal 12-molecule ball and dual K_t. Complete symbolic enumeration of affine constraint intersections gives the 18 interior dual vertices; the 28 norming pairs produce the numerical-radius maximum. The D4 group reduces all 108 operator-norm tensors to ten absolute-value orbits and ten explicit norming-functional decompositions prove the global lower bound. Two fully explicit operators realize the respective sharp bound on [1,sqrt(2)] and [sqrt(2),2]. Full-interval inequalities are verified by exact critical-point algebra and the crossing factorization (2-t)^2(t^2-2)/t^3; endpoints follow from continuity of finite-dimensional norms. The standalone verify.py was run successfully. Symbolic calculations corroborate an explained finite exact proof, not unbounded sampling.

value.rationale: The snowflaked 4-cycle is a canonical one-parameter metric deformation between the equilateral 4-point space and the cycle shortest-path metric. The result classifies its intrinsic real numerical index over the entire interval, proves exact sharpness with two nonidentical operator witnesses, and isolates a genuine phase transition at the natural exponent 1/2 even when facet counts are constant. It is a structural nonlinear change in operator norm-versus-numerical-radius behavior, not a single arbitrarily selected parameter or textbook substitute.
